feedback.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 \\ 2 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the coordinates of the point ${C}^{′}$, the image of $C(0,3)$ under the action of $T?$

${C}^{′}($ 
{{field-1}},
{{field-2}}$)$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the image of $C$ under the action of $T$, we first create a column-vector $x$ containing the coordinates of $C:$

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $x$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $Tx:$

$$
\begin{aligned}Tx & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 \\ 2 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The result, $Tx,$ contains the coordinates of ${C}^{′}.$ Therefore, ${C}^{′}(0,-12).$
